transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello — do you have any questions about your cataract surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi! Yes, I do have a few questions. First off, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can go back to light gardening after 1 week. Try to avoid heavy work. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Great, thank you. I was also wondering when I can start using my eye gel for dry eyes again?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: If you were using eye drops or eye gel before your operation for dry eyes, it is safe to continue using them unless you were told otherwise. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That's helpful, thanks! I'm also finding that I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: A bit of light sensitivity can be normal while the eye adjusts to the new lens. If it’s just mild, wearing sunglasses outside can help. But if the light sensitivity is severe, or if your eye is red and painful too, that is not normal and we may need to check it. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That makes sense, I'll keep an eye on it. One more question—should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Yes, it can be normal for vision not to be completely clear in the first week after the operation. It should improve quickly and settle down over time. If it’s still blurry, or getting worse, we may need to check it. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, I think that's everything I needed to know. Thanks so much for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have all your questions been answered?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, all my questions have been answered. Thank you for your assistance!

verdict.label: pass
